body:
Could you provide profiling data or benchmarks for this change?

Modern CPU architectures (x86_64/ARM) routinely handle 96-bit (12-byte) types in registers (SIMD/vector).

Passing this by `const&` can force the compiler to pass a pointer under the hood (depending on whether inlined or optimized), introducing memory indirection and potential pointer aliasing issues that hurt optimization.

As a general rule of thumb for modern hardware:
* up to 64-bit: Always pass by value.
* up to 256-bit: Benchmark both, but value is frequently faster due to register allocation and lack of aliasing.
 
Given our mixed 32-bit/64-bit `real_t` considerations, we shouldn't assume references are faster here without concrete numbers.

...

Also there's a real danger of "re-arranging deck chairs on the titanic" here. One person swaps to `const ref` _on principle_, another profiles, finds value is faster, then repeat.

I guess imo if we were to want to go ahead with this kind of thing, we would agree in a core meeting on some kind of standard here, I don't know if we have it in our coding standards doc. (_if indeed we are to go about this kind of change, I know some prefer to leave this kind of decision up to the original author_).

Unless it's hot code, in which case standards go out the window. :wink:
